uniqueNotes: The United States is not on China’s 30-day unilateral visa-free list. A standalone holiday usually needs a tourist (L) visa before travel.
US passport holders can use the 240-hour (10-day) visa-free transit policy when flying to a confirmed third country via an eligible Chinese port — not for a simple round-trip US–China–US itinerary.
US emergency (limited-validity) passports are generally not accepted for visa-free or transit visa-free entry; apply for a visa if you travel on an emergency passport.
commonRoutes: Many US travelers enter via Shanghai (PVG), Beijing (PEK/PKX), Guangzhou (CAN), or Chengdu (TFU), often connecting onward to Southeast Asia, Japan, or Korea under 240-hour transit rules.
